items.stem: Under IAS 1, which heading comes immediately after gross profit in a published income statement?
items.answer: Distribution costs and administrative expenses
items.markingKey: Revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, distribution costs, administrative expenses, profit from operations [1].

items.stem: Explain why companies are required to publish financial statements in a standard format such as IAS 1.
items.answer: Standard formats make statements comparable between companies and over time, give users consistent and reliable information and help prevent misleading presentation.
items.markingKey: Comparability [1]; reliability/consistency for users [1]; prevents manipulation [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why a proposed final dividend at the year end is not shown as a liability in the statement of financial position.
items.answer: Under IAS 10 the dividend is not an obligation until approved by shareholders after the reporting date, so it is disclosed in a note only.
items.markingKey: Not a present obligation at year end [1]; disclosed by note (IAS 10) [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why notes to the financial statements are useful to shareholders.
items.answer: They give detail behind the totals (e.g. PPE movements, borrowings, contingencies) and explain policies, so users can understand, compare and assess the figures.

items.stem: Complete the statement: In the indirect method, depreciation is …

items.answer: added back to profit from operations

items.stem: Explain why a profitable company may still have a decrease in cash and cash equivalents.
items.answer: Profit is not cash: cash may be spent on non-current assets, inventory build-up, increased receivables, loan repayments or dividends, none of which reduce profit.
items.markingKey: Profit ≠ cash (accruals) [1]; two examples [2] [3]

items.stem: Explain two uses of a statement of cash flows to a lender.
items.answer: Shows ability to generate cash from operations to pay interest and repay loans; reveals how investment was financed and whether liquidity is improving.
items.markingKey: Two uses [1 each] with explanation [1 each] [4]

items.stem: Distinguish between the role of the directors and the role of the external auditor in relation to the financial statements.
items.answer: Directors prepare the statements and are responsible for their accuracy and for internal controls (stewardship); auditors independently examine them and report an opinion to shareholders.
items.markingKey: Directors prepare/responsible [1]; auditors independent opinion to shareholders [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the meaning of "true and fair view".
items.answer: True: free from material error and factually correct; fair: presented objectively without bias, in accordance with accounting standards.
items.markingKey: True explained [1]; fair explained [1] [2]

items.stem: The auditor of Ibis plc uses a materiality threshold of 10% of profit before tax, which is $280,000. items.markingKey: Materiality = 10% × $280,000 = $28,000 [1]; $17,500 is not material [1]; opinion: unmodified [1]

items.stem: Explain why the independence of the external auditor is important.
items.answer: Shareholders rely on the opinion; if the auditor has financial or personal links with the company the opinion may be biased and the credibility of the statements is lost.
items.markingKey: Users rely on opinion [1]; conflict of interest causes bias [1]; credibility [1] [3]

items.stem: The plant and machinery of Vanguard Ltd at the start of the year: cost $690,000, accumulated depreciation $187,000. During the year machines costing $84,000 were bought. items.stem: Monarch plc reports revenue of $1,010,000 and gross profit of $354,000 for the year ended 30 June 2026. items.stem: In the draft statement of cash flows of Osprey Ltd, the increase in inventories of $12,000 was added in reconciling profit from operations to cash generated from operations. Explain the error and calculate its effect on the reported cash generated from operations.
items.answer: The increase in inventories should be deducted. Cash generated from operations is misstated by 2 × $12,000 = $24,000 (overstated).
items.markingKey: Correct treatment (deducted) [1]; reason linked to cash [1]; effect $24,000 overstated [1] [3]

items.stem: In the draft statement of cash flows of Monarch plc, the depreciation of $23,500 was deducted in reconciling profit from operations to cash generated from operations. Explain the error and calculate its effect on the reported cash generated from operations.
items.answer: The depreciation should be added. Cash generated from operations is misstated by 2 × $23,500 = $47,000 (understated).

items.stem: The auditor of Monarch plc uses a materiality threshold of 10% of profit before tax, which is $840,000. The directors refuse to correct a receivable from a customer who is now insolvent of $44,500. items.answer: Threshold $84,000; misstatement is not material; unmodified opinion
